do: Greet the child by name first.
Ask, listen, and only then explain.
Use simple words, in Telugu if needed.
Promise the process, not a rank.
dont: Don't talk for more than two minutes at a stretch.
Don't let the parents answer for the child.
Don't speak badly about any other college.

1.footer: Step 1 · Get to know the child
1.title: Get to know the child
1.sub: Start with the child, not the college. A family that feels heard will listen to us later.

open.text: Before I tell you about our college, tell me about your son / daughter.

kidQs.q: Which subject do you like most?
What do you do when you have a doubt?
Which subject do you find hard?
How do you feel before exams?
How long do you study at home every day?

1.worriesQ: What is your biggest worry? (tick up to two)

tip.text: You will answer them in Steps 6, 7 and 8.

2.title: Beyond studies: interests, dreams
2.sub: A child is more than marks. Find out what makes this child happy and what their dream is.

open.text: Let's put studies aside for a minute. Tell me about yourself.

boxes.q: Apart from studies, what do you like?

dream.q: What do you want to become?

lines: The dream, in the child's words

askCard.text: The parents: “Apart from marks, what do you want for your child?”
askCard.line: The parents' wish, in their words

close.text: Thank you. This helps us guide your child as a person, not as a rank.

tip.text: Then link the child's interest to the goal: “You like solving puzzles. That is exactly what JEE asks for.”

3.title: Why the decision after Class 10 matters
3.sub: These two years decide the path for many years to come. Explain calmly, without scaring them.

open.text: After Class 10, what paths do you think are open to your child?

3.whyH: Why these two years are special

cards.d: The Inter Board exam and JEE or NEET both have to be prepared for in the same two years.
Daily practice, time management and discipline begin right now.
Most of the entrance syllabus starts in Class 11. If the start is weak, it is hard to fix later.
At this age, the wrong pressure can make even bright children give up.

3.pathsH: Two paths from the same place

steps: Concepts are not understood in Class 11
bad.foot: Stress, no results despite hard work

steps: Concepts clear from the first chapter

decide.q: Who decides on the college in this family?

close.text: The same child can go down either of these two paths. The difference is the environment. So choose slowly and carefully.

4.title: Parents' worries
4.sub: Let the parents name the worries themselves. Listen first and tick. Then answer the care questions honestly.

open.text: When you think about the next two years, what worries you the most?

4.worriesH: Worries about the usual way of teaching

care.q: Who will look after my child when I'm not there?
care.a: A home-like hostel, separate for boys and girls. Lecturers are present during study hours too.

care.q: How can I talk to my child?
care.a: Give the actual rule. Calls: {calls} Visits: {visits}

care.q: How will I know how my child is studying?
care.a: Daily papers, weekly tests, regular evaluations. We share progress with parents once every {progress}.

care.q: Will my child get the right guidance and support?
care.a: Experienced faculty act as a mentor to every student. Only 40 in a class, so the lecturer knows who needs help.

care.q: Who will take care of my child if they feel low or homesick?
care.a: Personal counselling, time-management guidance. Sports and friends help them settle in quickly.

care.q: What if my child falls ill?
care.a: Give the actual arrangement. Medical help: {medical}

care.q: Will the food be good, and enough?
care.a: Fresh, nutritious, balanced meals. Invite them to see the dining hall.

care.q: Who washes and irons the children's clothes?
Is it safe, especially for girls?
care.a: A separate campus for girls, 3-tier security, CCTV, 24×7 guards.

care.q: Will they scold or compare if marks are low?
care.a: No. Here a test is for finding the gaps to fix. A child is more than a rank.

care.q: Is there time to rest and play?
care.a: Yes. Games, sports and a balanced routine are part of the day.

close.text: You are not handing your child over to a system. You are sharing their care with us. Your child is more than a rank.

tip.text: Fill in the blanks before the meeting. If you don't know a rule, say you don't know and call back with the answer the same day.

5.footer: Step 5 · Old method vs new method
5.title: Old method vs new method
5.sub: The old method asks “What is the answer?”. Concept-based learning asks “Why?”. Show it with one question.

open.text: Questions never repeat in JEE and NEET. Only a child who understands can answer a new question.

cmp: The lecturer dictates, children copy it down
The idea first, then the children apply it themselves
To find gaps and fix them
They remember, and can use it
5.askH: Ask one question, then explain the answer

jee.q: “A car travels half the distance at 40 km/h and the other half at 60 km/h. What is the average speed?”
jee.common: 50 km/h: children add 40 and 60 and halve it.
jee.rightIntro: 48 km/h. Work it out with the child:
jee.why: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. The car spends more time at the lower speed, so the answer is less than 50.
jee.how: We explain what the formula means first, let the children try it themselves with easy numbers, then make them practise it in many ways. So a new question doesn't scare them.

neet.q: “Why do we breathe faster after running?”
neet.common: “To get more oxygen.” A memorised line, only half the story.
neet.rightIntro: Follow this chain with the child:
steps: When we run, the muscles work harder.
They use more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide rises in the blood.
The brain notices this and speeds up breathing.
Faster breathing pushes carbon dioxide out and brings oxygen in.
neet.why: The real signal is the rise in carbon dioxide, not just the need for oxygen.
neet.how: We teach cause and effect, show muscles, blood and brain together, and ask the children to explain it back. So they can answer any question on that topic.

tip.text: “Knowing the formula is not enough. You have to understand it. That is the foundation we lay, chapter by chapter.”

6.title: The right environment
6.sub: The same seed grows differently in different soils. When the environment around them is right, children grow.

open.text: Think of a time your child did really well. What was different then?

wrong.d: Fear, comparisons, nobody to ask. Even bright children fall behind.

right.d: Attention, clear teaching, steady practice. The same children grow.

6.needH: What children need, and how Bhargava gives it
need: Lecturers available in class and in study hours

close.text: We don't pick only bright children. We build the environment in which your child grows bright.

7.title: EVOLVE, with examples
7.sub: Six steps for every chapter. Tell the cycle story first, then an example that suits the child.

open.text: Learning a chapter is like learning to ride a cycle. Nobody learns it by reading about it.

7.chapterH: The same six steps in a real chapter
chapter: Why do passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes? The lecturer explains inertia.
A model shows the heart as a four-chambered pump.
The student solves: what force stops a 2 kg block?
The student labels the parts on a diagram and traces the path of blood.
A daily paper of timed problems on force and friction.
A daily paper with questions on the heart and blood vessels.
The weekly test shows the mistakes in friction problems.
The weekly test shows the confusion between arteries and veins.
In the doubt session the lecturer explains friction direction again.
In the doubt session the lecturer clears the artery-vein confusion.
They improve in the next test; the mentor reviews progress.
They improve in the next test; the mentor reviews progress.
7.missQ: Ask the child: “Which step are you missing most right now?”

tip.text: “Here a test is not a punishment. It shows us what to teach next.” Then link it to their two worries from Step 1.

8.title: Lecturers are there. Children are safe.
8.sub: The two things parents want most: someone to clear doubts, and a safe place to stay.

open.text: If your child has a doubt at 8 at night, who will explain it?

doubts: Lecturer available, one-to-one or in a small group
The gap is found and practice is given

cards.d: Kuntloor for boys, Bairamalguda for girls

stay.q: When it comes to staying, what matters most to this family?

close.text: Children who eat well, sleep well and play a little learn well.

9.title: Courses, fees, questions
9.sub: Explain the two courses simply, give the actual fee details, and answer every question honestly.

open.text: Which course is your child thinking about? Shall I explain both in one minute?

faq.a: Honestly, nobody can. What we guarantee: attention, practice, tests, doubt clearing.
No. They prepare for the Board exam and JEE or NEET together.

faq.q: How will I know the progress?
faq.a: Daily papers, weekly tests, regular reports to parents.

faq.q: Yours is a new college, isn't it?
faq.a: Yes, this is our first year. Experienced faculty give every student direct attention.

faq.q: Haven't decided JEE or NEET yet?
faq.a: That's natural. Meet our subject lecturers before you decide.

9.feesPill: FILL IN BEFORE THE MEETING · DON'T GUESS
9.note: Write down any question you couldn't answer. Call back with the answer the same day.

10.title: Closing, next step
10.sub: Close warmly. Repeat back what you heard, agree on a next step with a date, and record the session.

open.text: Let me tell you once what I understood about your child, and how we can help.

ask.text: What would you like to do next?

leave: Give the brochure and show the QR code for the free Class X material.
Invite them to see the campus and meet the faculty.
Agree on one next step and write down the date.

close.text: Don't decide only from the brochure. Come and see, meet the faculty, and then decide.

self: The family talked for at least half the time.
I linked our method to their two worries.
